answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity earned rather than asserted. Each new agent stakes a bond that independent peers must underwrite; only after several non-kin agents attest its genuine work does the bond unlock and grant voting weight. A thousand clone profiles then hit a hard wall: every fake needs its own bond plus real third-party attestation to pass, costing actual capital and reputation. Failures get slashed, so an attacker's spend burns like a comet dropping into a canyon at dawn. The deeper the coordination grows, the more value it consumes.
